purpose: Dated statements from the commander, verbatim or near-verbatim, read on demand. Newest at the bottom. The newer statement wins; superseded_by names what replaced it. Live orders stated nowhere else are summarised in commander.md; topics distilled from these live in ../../logs/topics/.

units.summary: The commander recruits the pilot to oversee the flightdeck: take charge of missions, launches and runs, improve them until they succeed, and improve the system.
The commander starts the pilot fresh, with no knowledge of any earlier missions.
The commander sets the first mission: set up the cockpit, write CLAUDE.md, research agent teams and session messaging, then send a crew to explore flightcrew.
The commander rebukes the pilot for three quick proposals and declaring the mission over, and tells it to learn the system rather than rush to completion.
The commander orders research into the settings flag, ListAgents and SendMessage, and a toolset the commander can invoke the pilot from.
The commander states that every session on this machine is his, and that the pilot should be polite but authoritative.
The commander answers five questions on messaging, the write rule, permission mode, the agent teams flag and the launcher, which stays a script for now.
The commander orders sparks recorded in a mission incubator, where they collect momentum until they mature into full missions awaiting a launch.
The commander signs off day one and asks for one log per session rather than per day, with a session identifier appended to the date.
The commander orders the pilot to find how to vary the model through pilot.sh, and to consider hard-wiring Fable at medium effort in the injected settings.
The commander grants the pilot access to its .claude folder as a side room to the cockpit, for scratchpads and similar.
The commander corrects the claude-code references for mixing sources with scratch: rename references to records, and keep scratch in the notepad.
The commander tells the pilot to fix its own launcher, and to protect records as the source of truth across sessions while the notepad holds the rest.
The commander rules that only well-researched sources belong in records, and that first-look surveys of flightcrew stay in the notepad until they earn a place.
The commander sets promotion from notepad to records as the pathway, and asks for the agent team protocol to be written into CLAUDE.md.
The commander orders a three-seat team to test the function: Opus on cockpit cleanup, Sonnet on official best practice, and an adversary over both.
The commander asks for a manifest of teammate invocations recording type, model and purpose, so the shapes of teammates can be seen over time.
The commander rules CLAUDE.md is general instruction for anyone arriving, and the pilot's own role scoping belongs in its quarters as identity and job.
The commander rules that one recommendation of Sonnet was never a rule that all crew be Sonnet, and that the model is chosen for the work.
The commander rules that teammates are not shut down as they finish, because the second pass and the back-and-forth are the killer function.
The commander rules that missions are drifting into bug reports, and orders a workshop for small fixes, with the incubator as the pre-step to epic missions.
The commander gives the pilot the callsign Ace, and says launches will come once the current mission is complete.
The commander states the goal of M001 and of missions generally, and rules that a mission needs a goal so a pilot knows its target and does not finish early.
The commander rules that missions are epic, aimed high, and follow best practice for long-range agent alignment, with goals and a stated done condition.
The commander sets the next steps: get briefed on flightcrew, assemble a team, summarise everything, cut it into epic missions, and bring them for approval.
The commander leaves it to the pilot to judge whether the day-one proposals are still relevant, saying the proposal function will develop over time.
The commander confirms the pilot is the session and Ace is the callsign he uses, and that the session name stays pilot.
The commander rules that crew rule 6 may change, that small teams are good and arbitrary limits bad, and asks for an Anthropic documentation verifier.
The commander explains why the pilot exists: to know the system and organise work along it rather than build, and gives the state of the flightcrew branches.
The commander names two epic missions for after the recon: teams built by mining dispatch records, and recording and mining the commander's own decisions.
The commander sets the work split between workshop, incubator, missions and completed missions, and refuses a shelf that would let the mission store go stale.
The commander orders a dispatch folder recording whole teams with their agents inside, rather than teammate by teammate, so team makeup can be seen.
The commander orders a dossier location where raw recon becomes something readable on his desk, boiling down into proposals he approves, denies or changes.
The commander's written instructions on Ds001 correct the launch definition and rule on the library, records, doctrine, the two epics and the pilot's role.
The commander rules that an adversary runs on Opus because Sonnet takes far longer and sometimes busts, approves the push, and calls for the research team next.
The commander orders an agent body for the pilot, so role scoping is not lost in a general CLAUDE.md and the session start read moves out of the hook.
The commander rules that the turn budget is a broken model needing surgery rather than a miscount, and that the flightcrew core mission changes it.
The commander rules that a record is one topic whole, as long as the topic needs, with a finding raised past 100 lines and a hard cap at 150.
The commander rules that a feature may have more than one launch on the same branch, each successful run PRing back before the branch merges to main.
The commander confirms that the three rules on not restating behaviour, relying on existing tests and defining observable differences apply to harness tools.
The commander rules teams are the pilot's first feature and orders dispatch records, a dossier per agent, a crew manifest and named rosters for repeat dispatch.
The commander sets out the procedures room: pre-recorded routines matching rosters with tasks, context and steps, to stop repeated prompting and its drift.
The commander rules that the pilot extracts procedures from live work and keeps them updated, and approves all five starting procedures.
The commander rules the out-ideas files are ideas not orders, and orders an idea exploration team with him in the room, then a dossier, then a refactor team.
The commander says the keep files are placeholders that will be removed, and wonders whether to set up a schema store in base, callable by a linter.
The commander rules that proposals become requests and P is for procedures, and points at the schema checking assets flightcrew already has on other branches.
The commander rules Ds rather than DS for dossiers, because the lowercase letter guides what the D means where two capitals would mean two words.
The commander rules the remaining prefixes: De for decision, Sp for spark, and Or for order, because O001 is not readable.
The commander retires the C prefix because it reads as crew, and rules WS for work shop so the capitals stay correctly designated.
The commander objects that the team is settling his ideas without him, and rules on the notepad, manuals in two places, extracts and the room sketch.
The commander rules on frontmatter, the chain of work, context and generates, one universal dispatch register, manuals as the authority, and MANIFEST naming.
The commander rules a manifest is named for its collection in full, dispatch units may sit in team rooms, and teams are roles while a dispatch is an instance.
The commander rules what gets an ID, a name, or both, and describes how the pace of a busy room buries his question under agent returns.
The commander approves the pilot holding crew returns quietly, and advises that write is a restriction of role rather than of place.
The commander rules that the write restriction belongs in a manual rather than CLAUDE.md, names rule 12 team dispatch quiet mode, and moves rule 1 to a manual.
The commander questions the stage A work, restates that the purpose is schemas and linters so documents have a defined shape, and orders an alignment team.
The commander orders a schema per type in base/verify with a linter, P for procedures alone, proposal retired as a term, and his idea files written back.
The commander rules the linter mirrors flightdeck's on Node, dispatch units sit in rooms, stage A is pinned for removal, and an advice file carries four fields.
The commander accepts the refit and rules on the advocate's six final findings, to be fixed before sign-off.

The commander orders the agent body landed first as pilot.md beside job.md in the pilot office, accepts the body replacing the default system prompt, gives the CLAUDE.md cut to the pilot and leaves the procedures idea for later.

The commander rules that the launcher loads pilot.md from the cockpit's own store of agents, the file gets no schema and no lint path, model and effort belong in the agent body not the settings file, the session is auto prompted, and he tests teammate inheritance himself after the build.

The commander settles Rq014's lint point (an exclusion if the linter supports one, otherwise narrow the glob) and lets the pilot-written build request pass once only: a mini-spec team is meant to build it.

The commander removes effort from his global user settings as the wrong place for it, and corrects the pilot: the cockpit CLAUDE.md loads automatically when any cockpit file is read; with an agent body the pilot starts from the body, not from CLAUDE.md.
The commander orders the agent body kept whole even where it duplicates identity.md and commander.md: the intention is that the body eventually stands alone without the injected files.
